agent_response.summary: Candidate 1 changes how the signal and noise solves step through the frequency axis. The work after the carrier solve (signal assembly, carrier scaling, conjugation, signal solve, the A^H noise-weight solve, noise-matrix update and covariance solve) is now in `_signal_and_noise`. It runs one frequency at a time through lax.map (`FREQUENCY_CHUNK_SIZE = 1`) instead of as one vmapped batch of 101. Detector-selection preparation does not depend on frequency, so it is now computed once before the loop, with the same operations. A last partial chunk is padded by repeating the last row, and those extra results are thrown away. The full vmap still runs when the chunk size is None, when the carrier batch is not 1, or when there are no more frequencies than the chunk size. Nothing was run locally: no syntax check, no local run and no timing, so the candidate is untested until the screen.
agent_response.hypothesis: Running one frequency at a time works on about 9 MB per matrix instead of materializing many ~0.91 GB (101×751×752 complex128) intermediates. These are the scatter, carrier scaling, conjugation where, astype and explicit A^H transpose. That may cut memory traffic and page-fault cost, lowering first forward execution (11.5 s in the parent) and peak RSS (12.5 GB in the parent). Compile time should stay about the same because the loop body is traced once. Gradient compile and run time may change because the reverse pass becomes a reverse scan. The total amount of residual data saved for the gradient is unchanged. The signal and covariance solves on the same matrix A are inside the same loop body, so any existing reuse of their factorization is kept. No factorization is shared between A and A^H. Results per frequency should be mathematically identical. Batch-1 dot/einsum may round slightly differently, and the strict comparison must confirm whether that matters.
agent_response.notes: Notes are in experiments/notes/claude-frequency-batching.md: parent, source evidence, hypothesis, the proposed operator and the candidate log. Parent: 6dc993a06cf2de5ae2ae3afa83304a46b2ead4d0, run 80863bdee23a48d2b000e3b32e481ecc, first-run 24.657 s. Proposed operator: frequency_chunk_size with values {None, 1, 4, 8, 16}, default None until measured. It is a module constant read at trace time, so the benchmark's inputs and its three JIT stages are unchanged. 101 is prime, so any chunk size other than 1 or 101 has a remainder. lax.map(batch_size=) would trace the loop body a second time for it, so this code pads instead (single trace, about 3% wasted solves for k=8). Risks: copying saved gradient data into the loop's stacked buffers, a slower reverse scan, and rounding differences at batch size 1. Next: if the screen and full runs show lower forward time or memory and strict passes, try k=4 or 8. If forward or gradient time gets worse, try k=16 or record why chunking doesn't help.
